rules.title: Restriction on certain magnets, tantalum and tungsten
rules.applies_when: You deliver items to the US Department of Defense, directly or as a subcontractor, and the contract includes DFARS clause 252.225-7052.
rules.scope_note: The restricted items are samarium-cobalt and neodymium-iron-boron magnets, and tantalum metals and alloys (also tungsten metal powder and heavy alloy, which CMSEI does not score yet). Raw rare earth or cobalt material is relevant only where it ends up in those magnets or metals.

dates.what: The restriction extends from melting and producing to the entire supply chain, from mining of the ore or feedstock through the finished magnet or metal.

sources.label: DFARS final rule, Federal Register, 30 May 2024

rules.title: Conflict minerals disclosure (Form SD)
rules.applies_when: You file reports with the SEC and tin, tantalum, tungsten or gold is necessary to the functionality or production of a product you make or contract to make.
rules.scope_note: Requires a reasonable country-of-origin inquiry and, where minerals may come from covered countries, due diligence and a report. Tungsten and gold are covered by the rule but not scored by CMSEI yet.

dates.what: Form SD is filed each year by 31 May for the previous calendar year.

rules.title: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, high-priority sectors
rules.applies_when: You import goods into the US that are mined, produced or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang, or by entities on the UFLPA Entity List. Origin in China alone does not trigger it. A link to Xinjiang does.
rules.scope_note: Bauxite feeds aluminum and lithium is a listed sector. Both are designated high-priority sectors for enforcement. The list changes, so check the current DHS strategy.

dates.what: Aluminum, PVC and seafood added as high-priority sectors.
Steel, copper, lithium, caustic soda and red dates added (per STR Trade Report; confirm on the DHS site).
